claim_checks.source: Theorem C p. 3; Definition 7.2-7.3 and Theorem 7.4 pp. 28-29; counterevidence pp. 29, 31-33
claim_checks.independent_reason: In D_infinity with r(x)=x+1 and s(x)=-x, r is loxodromic, WPD follows from bounded integer displacement, and projection r^m s^e -> r^m is valid. Distance to the axis is at most one, so the required far-axis condition with threshold two is vacuous under the actual definition. Word length |m|+e gives |B(n)|=4n and exactly 2n non-loxodromics for every n>=1. The single-domain HHG Z is normalized and has unbounded products vacuously; the actual external Definition 6.9 permits its cobounded line. D_infinity is quasi-isometric to Z with additive distance error at most one, and its non-Morse proportion is also 1/2.
claim_checks.counterevidence_and_impact: The later theorems explicitly exclude virtually cyclic groups. The broad printed C/7.4 do not. This is a counterexample to a principal universal quantitative guarantee and supports Major, while leaving the mapping-class-group statement and properly restricted extensions unrefuted.
